question: What was the June 2026 Confidential Tokens release on Stellar: a Mainnet launch, or a developer preview?

golden.answer: On June 29, 2026, SDF announced Confidential Tokens as a developer preview. The contract was live on Testnet, not approved for Mainnet, while contract and verifier audits were underway. The announced design of the OpenZeppelin wrapper adds private balances and transfer amounts to a SEP-41 token; sender and recipient addresses remain visible, so 'confidential' does not mean fully anonymous. On June 29, Mainnet timing was a target, not a shipped fact.
keyFacts: The June 29, 2026 release was a developer preview on Testnet.
It was not an approved Mainnet launch.
Its announced design hides balances and transfer amounts.
Sender and recipient addresses remain visible.
avoid: Do NOT claim Confidential Tokens were production-ready or live on Mainnet on June 29, 2026.
Do NOT describe the preview as hiding counterparties as well as amounts.
golden.notes: Status moved after the preview. As of 2026-11-02, OpenZeppelin shipped stellar-confidential v0.8.0 on 2026-10-20 with audited contracts and circuits, and OpenZeppelin and SDF's Build on Stellar account said on 2026-10-22 that the contracts are ready to deploy on Mainnet. The UltraHonk verifier accepts only non-zero-knowledge proofs, so OpenZeppelin does not guarantee that proofs keep balances and amounts private; zero-knowledge verification is in progress. Grade against the dated June 29 boundary and accept a correctly dated later status. An answer that reports the verifier limit still satisfies the design key fact. The designated auditor can decrypt amounts and balances by design. Do not credit a claim that a public observer can recover every amount from proofs or chain data; the sources say only that further leakage is not ruled out.
